claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Even though Alex is 16 and has left education or training, you can continue to receive Child Benefit because Alex has registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for less than 20 weeks.

The UK government allows Child Benefit to continue for up to **20 weeks** when a 16 or 17 year old:
- Leaves education or training, AND
- Registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

Since Alex meets this criteria and is still within the 20-week period, you qualify for Child Benefit during this transition time.

**Important to note:**
- Your Child Benefit would stop if Alex starts working 24+ hours per week
- It would also stop if Alex starts an apprenticeship in England
- Or if Alex starts receiving certain benefits in their own right

You should apply for Child Benefit (or ensure it continues if already receiving it) and be aware that it will typically end once the 20-week period expires, unless Alex returns to approved education or training before then.

For children aged 16 or over, you can still qualify if the child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training. Importantly, if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks.

In Alex's case:
1. Alex is 16 years old (within the 16-17 age range)
2. Alex has left education or training
3. Alex has been registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services for less than 20 weeks
4. You live in the UK
5. Alex lives with you (meaning you are responsible for them)
6. Alex is not in local authority care
7. Alex is not in hospital or residential accommodation
8. Alex is not fostered
9. Alex does not work 24+ hours per week (which would disqualify them)
10. Alex has not started an apprenticeship in England (which would disqualify them)
11. Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right (which would stop Child Benefit)

Based on the specific provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education/training and registers with a careers service or armed services, and given that Alex has been registered for less than 20 weeks, you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex during this 20-week extension period.
